newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH CENTRAL BANK UPS OFFICIAL INTEREST RATES.
newsitem.headline: POLISH CENTRAL BANK UPS OFFICIAL INTEREST RATES.

text.p: The National Bank of Poland increased the lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and the discount rate by 2.5 points to 24.5 percent, effective on August 4, the central bank said on Friday.

"The main reason we decided to increase interest rates is because of the continuing fast pace of current account deficit growth in the first half of 1997," NBP chief Hanna Gronkiewicz-Waltz told a news conference.
She said that despite an ever-tighter monetary policy by the NBP since December 1996 the C/A and especially the trade gap had continued to grow too quickly.

"If this pace (of C/A gap widening) is sustained for a longer time it may endanger our external trade balance, which would in turn reduce real purchasing power, increase inflation and/or make a socially painful stabilisation process needed."
The central banker said the government's year-on-year 13 percent 1997 inflation target might not be met.
"The target was not endangered a month ago, but today one can say it is slightly endgangered," Gronkiewicz-Waltz said.

The rate rise follows last month's 1997 budget change which allowed the government to borrow an additional 2.5 billion zlotys from the NBP in order to help it maintain liquidity while financing its flood relief programme.

"The (government flood) credit decision was made too hastily...as (it was) an instrument which could be used at once," she said, adding that in Poland's situation other fiscal instruments, such as a flood tax, would be more appropriate.
Over the last three weeks Poland's suffered its worst flood disaster ever, which killed 54 people and placed nearly two percent of the entire country was underwater.
